This is you, and you're making a mistake.
Every time your knife slices an onion, it rips open thousands of tiny cells.
And inside them, there's a chemical weapon.
Enzymes mix with sulfur compounds and turn into a volatile gas.
And it floats straight up to your face.
When it hits your eyes, the gas irritates your nerves.
Your brain thinks you're under attack and triggers an emergency flush.
To avoid this, chill the onion and use a sharp knife.
Cold slows the reaction, and a sharp blade crushes fewer cells.
